title: Wat Pa Tam Wua — edit proposals
notes: I lightly cleaned obvious typos in the draft (its/it's, Vipassana, monastery, etc.) and kept your voice. Bigger editorial calls are proposals below — approve, reject, or leave feedback. Media slots are placeholders until you upload /Users/lukaskoebis/Downloads/monastery.

proposals.before: towards the end helped running the introduction sessions for new arrivals.
proposals.after: towards the end helped run the introduction sessions for new arrivals.
proposals.rationale: Small grammar fix; keeps the same meaning.

proposals.summary: Add one line naming the monastery + location up front
proposals.before: I spent 8 days in a Buddhist monastery in the north of Thailand.
proposals.after: I spent 8 days at Wat Pa Tam Wua, a Buddhist monastery in northern Thailand (near Mae Hong Son).
proposals.rationale: Title is the monastery name, but the first sentence currently only says 'a Buddhist monastery'. Naming it early helps people who skim.

proposals.before: I think on my last two nights I got into some kind of Jhana state.
proposals.after: I think on my last two nights I got into some kind of absorption that felt like what people describe as a Jhana state — I'm not confident enough in the terminology to claim it was the real thing.
proposals.rationale: Jhana is a loaded technical term; softening matches your 'I think' hedging and avoids overclaiming.

proposals.summary: Drop or reframe 'Buddhism is a philosophy not a religion'
proposals.before: Buddhism is a philosophy not a religion — but in Thai culture and many other cultures it became more of a religion (temples, …).
proposals.after: I mostly engaged with Buddhism as a philosophy / practice rather than a religion — though in Thai culture (and many others) it clearly functions as one (temples, …).
proposals.rationale: The absolute 'is not a religion' line is contested and easy to argue with. Framing it as how you engaged with it is harder to attack and more accurate to your experience.

proposals.summary: Add your Kindle reading list (you left this as '…')
proposals.before: (missing — draft had 'Here are some of the books I downloaded to my kindle: * …')
proposals.after:
Add a short bullet list under Takeaways. Suggested starter (edit freely):
• Why Buddhism Is True — Robert Wright
• The Little Book of Clarity — Jamie Smart
• Walk to be the Knower — Wat Pa Tam Wua
• Siddhartha — Hermann Hesse
(+ whatever else you actually downloaded)
proposals.rationale: You explicitly wanted a books section. I need the real Kindle list from you — please paste titles in feedback if approving.

proposals.summary: Expand the Why Buddhism Is True / modular mind paragraph
proposals.before: One part I found interesting is that the "mind" basically consists of a lot of independent parts — Robert Wright's Why Buddhism Is True goes into this via evolutionary psychology: modular minds, the illusion of a unified self, and how mindfulness can weaken the modules that generate craving and aversion.
proposals.after: Keep the current short version for now, OR expand with 2–3 concrete examples from Wright (e.g. the feeling of a CEO-self is an illusion; modules compete; mindfulness lets you see a craving arise without acting on it). I left a short bridge in so the post isn't unfinished — say if you want the longer version.
proposals.rationale: Your draft had 'explain some of the stuff from the book' but no specifics. Short bridge is live; longer version needs your preference.

proposals.summary: Move Stoicism comparison into its own short subsection
proposals.before: Inline under Takeaways as a brief bullet pair.
proposals.after: Add an h3 'Stoicism vs Buddhism' so it doesn't feel buried in the closing.
proposals.rationale: It's a clean standalone idea; currently it sits awkwardly between neuroscience and the China/London wrap-up.

proposals.before: 11 bullets (phone, content, meditation, yoga, food, journal, reading, project, sensual desires, loving kindness, community)
proposals.after: Keep ~6: phone/content, meditation, food/fasting, deep project, loving-kindness/community, re-read journal.
proposals.rationale: The list is good but long for a closing. Trimming makes the ending punchier. Easy reject if you want the full personal checklist.

proposals.summary: Add practical visit details (clothes, what to bring)
proposals.after: Optional short paragraph: white clothes required for guests, mosquito net/repellent useful, no need to book, donations on departure, English is spoken in teaching sessions.
proposals.rationale: Useful if this post doubles as a recommendation. Skip if you want it more reflective than practical.

proposals.summary: Confirm post date + whether to email Dave a slightly different version
proposals.before: Currently dated September 2026. Draft said 'Send to: Dave Fontenot'.
proposals.after: Keep one public blog version. Optionally send Dave the same link with a short personal note (not a separate page).
proposals.rationale: Checking date accuracy and that Dave is a recipient of the link, not part of the post body.

proposals.summary: Wire up photos + chanting audio once uploaded
proposals.before: Placeholder boxes for monk / mountain / bed / walking / chanting.
proposals.after: Replace placeholders with files from Downloads/monastery. Suggested order matches your draft markers.
proposals.rationale: Blocked on upload — please attach the folder contents in chat.

proposals.summary: Keep or cut the investing CTA at the end
proposals.before: Please reach out if you have other reading recommendations, you're into these topics, or you're even building a company in that space (I'd love to invest!).
proposals.after:
Option A (keep): as written.
Option B (softer): drop the investing line and just ask for reading recommendations / people into the topics.
proposals.rationale: Fits your site (you invest), but some readers find it abrupt after a monastery post. Your call.
